title: Evaluation of ML-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool to Replace an Existing Tool in an Academic Health System: Lessons Learned
summary: A hospital implementation study compared a machine-learning clinical decision-support tool with its predecessor and assessed care outcomes. The authors reported a modest fall reduction after implementation; before/after evidence does not isolate the tool’s causal effect.
ai_technology: Hospital implementation study evaluates an ML clinical decision-support tool against the prior tool and care outcomes.
organization: Department of Medicine, Duke University School of Medicine, Durham, NC 27708, USA

evidence.tested: Results reports modest fall reduction after implementation with attribution limitations; before/after evidence, not causal proof.
evidence.unknown: The before/after design cannot attribute the observed falls change solely to the decision-support tool.
evidence.ai_role: Hospital implementation study evaluates an ML clinical decision-support tool against the prior tool and care outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
